title: Capacity hedging and slow-roll journal
content:
Objective:
- Capture an operational thinking journal for slow-rolls that explicitly hedges for capacity surprises (spikes, cold-cache KVs, model swap CPU variance). Use as my day-of checklist + quick reference. Not a final runbook, but a pragmatic, small-scope working doc.

Context / motivation:
- Recent dedicated rollout hit a transient token-cost/latency spike when cohort reached ~18% of traffic. Root cause looked like cache warmup + one model shard getting overloaded. I want a repeatable set of hedges we can apply rapidly during canary increases.
- This doc focuses on: pre-warming, fractional weight hedging, concurrency knobs, soft-fallbacks, and human triggers for pause/rollback.

Assumptions:
- We are doing a slow-roll from 0% -> 50% in 6 steps (0,1,3,10,25,50). Each step is planned for 30-90m observation windows.
- Serving runtime supports: per-route weights, region overrides, model-variant fallback, concurrency limits per pool, and KV-prefix warm cache API.
- Observability: token latency P50/P95/P99, queue length, model GPU UTIL, tail-latency CPU spillover, error-rate, cost per token (approx).

Primary hedges (short descriptions):
1) Capacity cushion (pre-commit)
   - Reserve a small burst pool: create a tiny reserved slot (2-4 GPUs equivalent) in the dedicated pool for the canary path. This is pre-allocated for the entire slow-roll window. Purpose: absorb short bursts and give us headroom while KV warms.
   - Action: infra request via ticket REL-371 to allocate 'canary-burst' pool.

2) Fractional hedging (traffic shaping)
   - When increasing weights, always route 5-10% of the intended increment to a cheaper variant or cached path for first 10 minutes: e.g., intended step 10% => 9% primary + 1% hedged (cached or quantized). Helps detect regressions early without full cost impact.

3) Soft-fallback routes
   - Configure immediate fallback to a stable model variant when latency exceeds threshold for N seconds. Fallback should be visible in routing logs and alert to on-call only when sustained > 10m.

4) Concurrency gating
   - Raise per-route concurrency gradually. Set starting concurrency to 0.5 * expected qps for cohort; increase by 25% every successful observation window. Prevents one shard from getting overloaded.

5) KV/prefix warm and progressive cache seeding
   - Use the internal warm-cache endpoint to push common prefixes used in production prompts for the canary cohort before the step. Seeding strategy: top 100 recent prompts (by freq) for that customer segment.

Signals to watch (quick list):
- P95 latency absolute (> 1.5x baseline)
- Error rate delta (> +0.3% absolute)
- GPU util skew (one machine > 80% while cluster avg < 50%)
- Queue length per pod / Bounded queue > 75% capacity
- Cost per token change > +20% vs baseline
- KV miss-rate rising during early minutes

Threshold-based actions (quick rules):
- If P95 > 1.5x baseline for > 5m: reduce canary by 50% and enable fallback variant. Notify oncall.
- If queue length > 75% for > 3m: pause progression and open extra burst capacity.
- If GPU skew observed: move 20% of traffic to other region/variant, tag for post-mortem.
- If error rate > 1% absolute: immediate rollback to previous stable and hotfix.

Quick CLI snippets (notes to self):
- Scale pool: infra-cli pools allocate --name canary-burst --gpu 2 --duration 6h
- Route adjust: routing-cli set-weight --route /generate --variant canary-v2 --weight 10
- Seed cache: curl -X POST https://internal-cache/seed -d @top100.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Check metrics: grafana?org=infra&var-route=/generate&range=15m

Observation window play (example day-of timeline):
- T0: Pre-warm cache + allocate canary-burst pool
- T0+10m: route 1% (hedged) -> watch 15m
- If OK -> T0+30m: route 3% (hedged) -> watch 30m
- If OK -> T0+90m: route 10% (9% primary + 1% hedged) -> watch 60m
- Continue: 25% -> 50% with same hedges (5%-10% hedged) and concurrency steps

Human playbook (who does what):
- Release lead (me): coordinate infra allocation, confirm baseline metrics, trigger weight changes
- Oncall SRE: monitor infra metrics, scale pools if needed, manage rollbacks
- Model owner: ready to toggle fallback variant and investigate quality regressions
- CS escalation: pre-alert for customers in cohort if we plan to pause for > 30m

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to automate hedged traffic allocation? (manual routing-cli today). Add a small automation ticket.
- Define exact seeding list generation: need a script to export top prompts for cohort by day.
- Should we bill hedged traffic differently in telemetry? Add flagged tag to traces for cost accounting.

Post-roll notes template (fill after every slow-roll):
- step, start_time, end_time, observed P95, errors, actions_taken, infra_changes, followups. (I will paste into REL-371)

Quick memory aids / heuristics (personal):
- "Hedge first, then scale" — always keep a small fraction on cheaper/cached path until P95 stabilizes for two windows.
- "Concurrency before weight" — prefer increasing concurrency cap before moving more traffic.

References and links I frequently check:
- Metric dashboards: /d/redwood-release/slow-roll-summary
- Past postmortem: REL-291-cold-cache-warmup
- Routing RFC: github.com/redwood/routing#hedged-early-exit

Notes to self (informal):
- If we get a weird one-off spike, try pausing for 5-10m rather than immediate rollback; sometimes KV warms in 7-12m.
- Keep a Slack message template ready: short summary, action taken, next steps. Save as macro.

End of journal. Will iterate after next slow-roll attempt.

---
choppy thoughts / fragments:
- consider a canary-specific autoscale policy (pre-warm CPU/GPU at 10% traffic to reduce cold-start penalties)
- think about a "cost-tag" on hedged traffic for post-facto chargeback
- capture response examples for quality checks during hedged routing (we currently only log latency/error, not content quality)
